from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex waves are like blended fruit smoothies.",
            "We can extract pure sine wave ingredients.",
            "This decomposition is a Fourier Series."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuitive Hook: The 'Smoothie' Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a complex 'smoothie' wave
        smoothie = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x) + 0.3 * np.sin(2*x) + 0.2 * np.sin(3*x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color="#008B8B")
        self.place_in_area(smoothie, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(smoothie))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#008B8B")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Deconstruct the smoothie into three simple sine waves
        sine1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color="#FF8C00")
        sine2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2*x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color="#EE82EE")
        sine3 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(3*x), x_range=[-PI, PI], color="#32CD32")
        
        self.place_in_area(sine1, 'D1', 'F2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(sine2, 'D3', 'F4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(sine3, 'D5', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(smoothie),
            Create(sine1),
            Create(sine2),
            Create(sine3)
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF8C00") # Coloring based on sequence start

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display a vibrating guitar string
        string = Line(start=np.array([-1, 0, 0]), end=np.array([1, 0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(string, 'B3', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(sine1), FadeOut(sine2), FadeOut(sine3),
            Create(string)
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Prerequisites: Orthogonality", [
            "Waves are vectors in function space.",
            "Orthogonality means they don't overlap.",
            "Think of perpendicular geometric axes."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualize two perpendicular vectors in bright blue (#00BFFF) and yellow (#FFFF00)
        vec1 = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=6).add_tip()
        vec2 = Line(ORIGIN, UP*1.5, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=6).add_tip()
        axes_group = VGroup(vec1, vec2)
        self.place_in_area(axes_group, "A1", "C3")
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a sine wave (orange #FF8C00) and a cosine wave (purple #9370DB)
        ax = Axes(x_range=[0, 2*PI, 0.5], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], axis_config={"include_ticks": False}).scale(0.5)
        sin_wave = ax.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color="#FF8C00")
        cos_wave = ax.plot(lambda x: np.cos(x), color="#9370DB")
        waves = VGroup(ax, sin_wave, cos_wave)
        self.place_in_area(waves, "D1", "F6")
        self.play(Create(ax), Create(sin_wave), Create(cos_wave))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#9370DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out overlapping parts, highlight 'cancellation'
        self.play(FadeOut(sin_wave), FadeOut(cos_wave))
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(axes_group, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Fourier Series Formula", ["The formula sums sine and cosine terms.", "Coefficients define the weight of each.", "Think of a digital equalizer."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The formula sums sine and cosine terms.
        fourier_formula = MathTex(
            "f(x) = \\frac{a_0}{2} + \\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty} (a_n \\cos(nx) + b_n \\sin(nx))",
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(fourier_formula, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(fourier_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Coefficients define the weight of each.
        # Ensure we pick up the sub-elements correctly
        a_n = fourier_formula.get_part_by_tex("a_n")
        b_n = fourier_formula.get_part_by_tex("b_n")
        
        # Yellow: #FFFF00, Orange: #FF8C00
        self.play(
            a_n.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            b_n.animate.set_color("#FF8C00"),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Think of a digital equalizer.
        # Use SVGMobject for equalizer icon as requested [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/equalizer.svg]
        # Color: cyan (#00CED1)
        equalizer_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/equalizer.svg")
        equalizer_icon.set_color("#00CED1")
        self.place_in_area(equalizer_icon, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(equalizer_icon))
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave", [
            "Adding harmonics builds complex shapes.",
            "Start with one simple sine wave.",
            "More terms create sharper edges.",
            "Watch the robotic hand trace corners.",
            "This is how functions converge."
        ])

        # Prepare wave functions
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-PI, PI], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)

        def get_wave(n_terms):
            return axes.plot(lambda x: sum([ (4/(np.pi*(2*k-1))) * np.sin((2*k-1)*x) for k in range(1, n_terms+1) ]), color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        wave1 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(wave1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        wave3 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + (1/3)*np.sin(3*x), color="#FFD700")
        self.play(Transform(wave1, wave3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#D8BFD8")
        wave7 = axes.plot(lambda x: sum([(4/(np.pi*(2*k-1))) * np.sin((2*k-1)*x) for k in range(1, 5)]), color="#D8BFD8")
        self.play(Transform(wave1, wave7))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#40E0D0")
        final_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: sum([(4/(np.pi*(2*k-1))) * np.sin((2*k-1)*x) for k in range(1, 20)]), color="#40E0D0")
        self.play(Transform(wave1, final_wave), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application and Conclusion: Signal Compression", [
            "Dominant coefficients capture the signal.",
            "We discard the noise for compression.",
            "Decompose, analyze, and then reconstruct."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Dominant coefficients capture the signal.
        # Represented as bars
        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=np.random.rand()*2+0.5, width=0.4, color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.8) for _ in range(5)])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B1", "C6")
        self.play(FadeIn(bars))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We discard the noise for compression.
        noise = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color="#808080", fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(self.grid["E1"] + np.array([i*0.3, 0, 0])) for i in range(10)])
        self.play(FadeIn(noise))
        self.play(FadeOut(noise))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Decompose, analyze, and then reconstruct.
        flow = VGroup(
            Text("Decompose", font_size=20),
            Arrow(RIGHT),
            Text("Analyze", font_size=20),
            Arrow(RIGHT),
            Text("Reconstruct", font_size=20)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(flow, "E3")
        self.play(Write(flow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Complex Waves

sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The 'Smoothie' Analogy
sections.content: Start with a complex periodic signal (the smoothie). Introduce the core concept: any periodic function can be decomposed into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves (the ingredients). Use a visual of a guitar string vibration to represent the pure harmonics.
sections.example: A chef (the mathematician) deconstructs a blended 'smoothie' signal back into its original 'fruit' components (sine waves).

sections.title: Mathematical Prerequisites: Orthogonality
sections.content: Briefly explain the 'dot product' of functions. Visualize why sine and cosine waves are independent (orthogonal) over a period, ensuring that when we extract a specific frequency, others 'cancel out' to zero.
sections.example: Represent orthogonal functions as perpendicular axes (X, Y, Z); just as you can't describe movement in Y using X, you can't represent a 3Hz wave using a 5Hz sine component.

sections.title: The Fourier Series Formula: The Anatomy of the Equation
sections.content: Present the formula f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos(nx) + bₙ sin(nx)). Explain that aₙ and bₙ are the 'weights' or 'strengths' of each harmonic component. Use animation to show the summation process.
sections.example: Imagine a digital equalizer on a music player: the coefficients aₙ and bₙ are the height of each frequency slider.

sections.title: Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave
sections.content: Demonstrate the 'Square Wave' example. Show an animation where we start with a single sine wave, then add the 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonics. Watch how the wave becomes sharper and more 'square' as more terms are added.
sections.example: A robotic hand (the partial sum) tracing a square path; more harmonics allow the hand to make sharper, more precise 90-degree corners.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion: Signal Compression
sections.content: Summarize how Fourier Series allows us to transmit or store data by keeping only the dominant coefficients. A quick recap of the 'Decomposition-Analysis-Reconstruction' flow.
sections.example: A bird singing: The Fourier Series identifies the core pitch and overtones, allowing us to compress the song file into a tiny format for streaming.
